newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: IATA gets connected for cyberspace flight bookings.
newsitem.headline: IATA gets connected for cyberspace flight bookings.

text.p: The global airlines body IATA, seeking to tap the booming Internet market, announced plans on Wednesday to recognise for the first time flight reservations by online service providers.

From August 1, the International Air Transport Association said service providers of electronic reservations would be allocated unique industry code numbers to enable airlines to identify their online bookings.

Requirements for the so-called Electronic Reservations Service Providers (ERSP) to receive IATA accreditation will be less strict than those for the world body's Accredited Travel Agents, it said in a statement.

Such online service providers handle reservation booking services for clients and may also offer some additional ticketing and payment possibilities if an airline allows them to do so, the Geneva- and Montreal-based IATA said.
The Internet -- specifically the world wide web of electronic mail and bulletin boards that connect personal and institutional computers -- has transformed the way airlines do business.
Traditional distribution costs including ticketing, commissions and marketing make up more than 20 percent of an airline's total costs, IATA says.
But recent industry studies say people still enjoy going to a travel agency, browsing through brochures and talking to agents as part of their vacation experience.
